title: Sales — Technical wins and fallback flow (WIP)
content:
Objective:
Short, skimmable deck for AEs and SEs to handle technical objections about latency, cost, and routing. Focus: concrete wins + exact fallback flow to keep apps live when capacity or SLAs are strained.

Audience:
- Primary: Sales Engineers (SEs) and Account Executives (AEs) during technical discovery/demo.
- Secondary: Solutions engineers and partner pre-sales.

One-line pitch for triage meeting:
"Redwood gives you predictable latency under real load and graceful fallbacks that preserve UX and cost — this doc gives the quick rebuttals + exact config knobs to use in a POC."

How to use this doc (quick):
- Read "Top 4 objections" section, memorize the first 2 bullets per objection.
- Use the demo script (page 3) to show deterministic behavior under simulated outage.
- If customer pushes for guaranteed latency, follow the "SLA vs cost handshake" flow and open GTM-4221 for dedicated capacity request.

Top 4 objections (short answers + notes):
1) "Your latency is inconsistent under load"
   - Quick answer: We provide latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) per route and automatic routing to lower-latency model variants when needed.
   - Tech note for SE: show token-level latency waterfall in Console (route → model variant → batch size) and the fallback trace (trace id: demo-trace-XXXX).
   - Demo tactic: run parallel load (use load script in linked artifacts) and flip on the canary fallback policy; show p99 drop.

2) "We need lower cost — can we use quantized models or cache results?"
   - Quick answer: Yes. Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles per workload and automatic prefix caching (per-user KV cache) that reduces token cost by 40% on chat-heavy flows.
   - Tech note: recommend quantize-16->8 profile for classification/embeddings; show sample cost delta table.
   - Demo tactic: toggle optimization profile in Console and show cost per 1k tokens projection.

3) "What happens if your region runs out of capacity?"
   - Quick answer: Smart routing will route to next compatible region or fall back to smaller model variant based on your policy. Customers can pin model versions for sensitive workloads.
   - Tech note: explain routing order: preferred-region → low-latency fallback region → compatible model variant → cold capacity (higher-latency).
   - Demo tactic: simulate capacity constraint by throttling a pool and show the automated fallback logs in Observability.

4) "We need enterprise controls / on-prem private deployment"
   - Quick answer: We support Private (VPC/on-prem) with customer-managed networking and KMS/HSM integration; fallbacks can stay internal per policy.
   - Tech note: capture the checklist to escalate to Solutions (see checklist below).

Decision tree (quick flow) — what SE should run during discovery:
- Does the customer require data to never leave VPC? → Yes: raise to Solutions + Private deployment track (linked_artifact CON-9876).
- Sensitive latency SLO (p95 < 150ms) for production? → Yes: recommend Dedicated capacity + baseline throughput commit; request capacity presizing (GTM-4221).
- Heavy chat workload with repeat prompts? → Enable prefix caching + recommend quantization profile.
- Cost-first (early stage)? → Show hosted cost projections and Enable burst autoscaling with cost cap.

Demo script (5–7 minutes):
- Setup: preloaded demo tenant (tenant-demo-redwood), two routes: chat-prod, chat-fallback.
- Step 1: show baseline p95/p99 with small load.
- Step 2: run simulated traffic (script: load-demo.sh — see linked artifacts).
- Step 3: flip canary fallback policy to "aggressive"; show in Console the model variant switch and p99 improvement.
- Step 4: show cost tab: before/after optimization profile.
- Step 5: if asked, open Console -> Observability -> trace -> show the tracing waterfall and where routing decision made.

Quick rebuttal snippets (copy-paste for Slack/email):
- "Latency spikes are predictable; we’ll show p99 before and after fallback policy in 5min with your sample trace id."
- "Quantization + prefix caching usually reduces token spend by ~30–50% for chat-like apps — we can run a quick cost projection for your rate card."
- "Private deployments keep data on-prem and allow you to keep fallbacks internal; we also support KMS for key control."

Config knobs to ask the customer for during discovery (exact names):
- routing.policies.primary_region (string)
- routing.policies.fallback_order (list)
- model.variants.default (id)
- optimize.quant_profile (enum: none, q8, q4_0)
- autoscale.burst_capacity (int)
- observability.trace_sample_rate (float)

Checklist to escalate to Solutions (if any true):
- SLOs: p95/p99 < target.
- Regulatory: data residency requirement.
- High throughput commit needed (> X tokens/s).
- On-prem or air-gapped requirement.
- Custom KMS/HSM integration.

Open questions / TODOs (for this doc):
- Add screenshots of Console flow for toggling fallback policies (TODO: Ethan to capture).
- Insert sample cost projection table for quantize-16→8 vs hosted baseline (TODO: Marina).
- Produce a one-button demo script hosted in examples repo (TODO: Ravi).

Links & quick refs (for SEs):
- Confluence: inference-fallbacks (CON-9876)
- Jira: GTM-4221 (dedicated presize request form)
- GH: examples/poc-fallback-demo (PR-318)
- Slack: #g2m-sequences (for ad-hoc help during live calls)

Appendix — short snippet for redwood Console commands (copyable):
- Toggle fallback policy via API:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/chat-prod/policy \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n    -d '{"fallback_mode":"aggressive"}'

- Sample call to simulate heavy load (local dev):
  ./load-demo.sh --target chat-prod --rps 120 --duration 60

Notes to self (voice memo style):
- Keep this deck to 2 slides (one-pager + demo script). Customers love short, actionable artifacts.
- Avoid heavy product jargon in AE-facing emails; use concrete numbers (p99, cost delta).
